item.title: Female leadership in public bureaucracies: Barriers, trajectories, and transformative Potential
item.content:encoded:
Michelle Fernandez, Universidade de Brasília

Fernando Nieto-Morales, El Colegio de México

This special issue examines female leadership in public bureaucracies, addressing persistent structural barriers limiting women's access to senior positions and the transformative potential of gender-diverse leadership. It seeks to understand how gender shapes governance and policy outcomes across diverse national contexts, particularly in Global South settings where gender inequalities intersect with institutional fragility.

While formal mechanisms like gender quotas and merit-based recruitment have expanded pathways for women, informal norms and implicit biases continue to perpetuate gendered hierarchies. The issue explores how institutional arrangements and organizational cultures shape women's trajectories and how female leadership influences accountability and sector performance.

The collection welcomes empirical contributions examining drivers and obstacles to women's leadership, factors shaping their careers, and policy impacts. Comparative perspectives, intersectional approaches, and research on Global South experiences are particularly encouraged.

Appel publié par Public Administration and Development. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gendered patterns of promotion in the public sector
  • Institutional reforms aimed at fostering gender parity in public leadership
  • Informal networks, mentorship, and the role of social capital in career advancement
  • Intersectional inequalities shaping women's leadership in government
  • The impact of female leadership on public service delivery and public policy
  • The effects of female leadership on public sector organizational culture and accountability

  • July 1, 2027: Deadline for full manuscript submissions

item.title: The Downsides of AI and Global Inequities: Why Good Governance Matters
item.content:encoded:
Yanto Chandra, City University of Hong Kong

Greta Nasi, Bocconi University

Jiasheng Zhang, Chinese University of Hong Kong

This special issue examines the negative consequences of AI adoption in public organizations, particularly how algorithmic systems can amplify existing inequalities and undermine democratic governance. The call recognizes that while AI offers potential improvements to service delivery, the benefits are unevenly distributed globally, with marginalized populations facing heightened risks related to biased datasets, algorithmic discrimination, and erosion of accountability.

The special issue seeks theoretical and empirical scholarship reconsidering how public administration frameworks must evolve to address AI-related challenges. Scholars are invited to investigate systemic downsides including workforce displacement, economic inequality, and uneven global access to AI innovations, as well as how governance mechanisms can embed fairness, transparency, and inclusiveness to protect democratic values and serve the public interest.

Appel publié par Public Administration and Development. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • North vs South disparities in AI access and innovation
  • Exploitation of labor in AI data collection and platform economies
  • Human rights implications of AI-driven decision-making
  • Accessibility to public services
  • The role of AI systems in perpetuating or challenging gender, racial, and cultural discrimination in public administration and welfare policies
  • Experiments on how citizens respond to diversity, inclusion and equity issues in the increasing use of AI by governments
  • Influence of dominant languages in AI training and its impact on linguistic diversity
  • How minority languages of the world can maintain their survival in the age of AI
  • Embedding fairness, transparency, and accountability into AI systems
  • Legal and regulatory frameworks for responsible AI deployment
